question: For each asserted world edge that never entered a served window, what does the evidence say: a recording gap, an alternate assertion path, an identity mismatch, or genuine assertion without service?
definition: A per-edge provenance ledger over the 26 rows in docs/presence_unexplained_edges.json. Categories are assigned in this order: recording gap (replay direct service exceeds committed direct service), identity mismatch (the reverse orientation was committed as served), alternate assertion path (a non-prediction structure carries the edge), genuine assertion without service (only a prediction candidate carries it and neither orientation was served).

source.assertion_sources: a behaviour-neutral replay of the same six Q4 on-arm cells; asserted fingerprint and served set must match

method: The same six Q4 seeds, 120 cycles, cap 40 and acquisition schedule are replayed to retain the final candidate types. The replay is accepted only when each seed's asserted-world fingerprint equals the stored Q4 fingerprint and its served-world set equals the committed N3 served set. No seed, arm, cap or treatment is added; the run is a provenance replay, not a new cell.

findings: All 26 edges reproduce their stored asserted fingerprint, and every seed's replay served-world set equals the committed N3 served set: no recording gap was observed.

18 edges have their endpoint pair served only in the reverse orientation; the reverse is itself a world edge, and the loop/dream readout is symmetric, so these are orientation/identity mismatches in the direct record, not proof that the directed edge was served.
8 edges were served in neither orientation and are carried by loop/dream structures: alternate assertion paths.
0 edges are carried only by a prediction candidate: the genuine assertion-without-service residual is empty on this block.
not_evidence: A provenance classification of one readout on six seeds, one world family, one build and one cap. It does not show why loop/dream structures carry these pairs, whether serving them would change A_W, or that any engine change is warranted. The reverse-orientation bucket is a record-identity description, not an engine defect.
